 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Two so-called small market baseball teams earning spots in the World Series caused a stir in the debate over MLB salary caps and the looming possibility of a lockout .
 While the Milwaukee Brewers are a small market compared to the Los Angeles Dodgers , the present-day Brewers are a monster compared to the last World Series squad Milwaukee sent up. According to Spotrac , the 2026 Brewers make a combined $140.7 million in total payroll allocations, excluding signing bonuses.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Without adjusting for inflation, there are seven Brewers players in 2026 who make more than the entire 1982 team: Christian Yelich, Brandon Woodruff, Dustin May, Antonio Senzatela, William Contreras, Andrew Vaughn and Jackson Chourio.
 Even after adjusting for inflation, Yelich's $26 million salary still eclipses the entire 1982 Milwaukee Brewers' combined salaries.
 More: Do the 1982 Brewers see a connection with the 2026 team? 
 The 1982 Milwaukee Brewers made a combined $6.4 million in 1982, according to The Baseball Almanac and Baseball References . The highest paid players were first baseman Cecil Cooper and catcher Ted Simmons , both paid about $1 million each.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Adjusted for inflation, Simmons and Cooper would make about $3.75 million each in 2026. That would land them between 2023-debut Brice Turang's $4.15 million salary and 2026-debut Cooper Pratt's $2.875 million per year.
 In 2026, the Milwaukee Brewers have the 19th-highest team salary out of the 30 MLB teams. The upcoming opponents, the Tampa Bay Rays , have the second-lowest team salary in the league at about $92 million.
 More: How costs have soared since the Brewers' last World Series in 1982

Some 400 fans were on hand to greet the team on its arrival. (Jack Orton, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) Kelly Kueng (left), Kim Spitzer and Shelly Geboy cheered the Milwaukee Brewers as the team arrived at Mitchell Field on Oct. 14, 1982, after Game 2 of the World Series in St. Louis. (Paul F. Gero, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) About 25,000 fans cheered for the Milwaukee Brewers during an old-fashioned pep rally and tailgate party Oct. 14, 1982, in a County Stadium parking lot. (Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) Cardinals outfielder Willie McGee makes a leaping catch as David Green watches at County Stadium in Game 3 of the 1982 World Series. (Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) Brewers pitcher Pete Vuckovich appeared to have a headache after giving up a three-run home run to the Cardinals' Willie McGee in the fifth inning during Game 3 of the World Series on Oct. 15, 1982. (Benny Sieu, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) Willie McGee of the St. Louis Cardinals leaped at the fence to catch a drive hit by Paul Molitor in the first inning of the Cardinals' 6-2 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the World Series on Oct. 15. 1982. (John E. Biever, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) Milwaukee Brewers manager Harvey Kuenn protests a call at first base in the second inning of Game 3 of the World Series game at County Stadium on Oct. 15, 1982. St. Louis won, 6-2, and has a 2-1 lead in the Series. (Benny Sieu, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) The Brewers' Gorman Thomas springs out of the batter's box after getting his clutch single in the seventh inning of Milwaukee's 7-5 victory in Game 4 of the World Series on Oct. 17, 1982. Thomas' single drove in the winning runs. (Ronald M. Overdahl, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) The Brewers' Bob McClure pitches in the ninth inning of Game 4 of the World Series on Oct. 16, 1982. (Benny Sieu, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) An aerial photo of Milwaukee County Stadium during the Game 4 of the World Series shows a County Stadium record 56,560 spectators, with the Goodyear blimp overhead, on Oct. 16, 1982. (Allan Y. Scott, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) Hearty food was downed by the Brewers after their victory over the St. Louis Cardinals in Game 4 of the World Series on Oct. 16, 1982. Jim Gantner and Rollie Fingers shared a rubdown table in the training room. Others eating beef sandwiches and drinking beer were (from left) Doc Medich (back to camera), Dwight Bernard, Mark Brouhard and Don Money. The Brewers are served "something to chew on" after every evening home game and between doubleheaders. (Richard Wood, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) Brewers outfielder Ben Oglivie can’t believe he was called out on a stolen-base attempt during Game 5 of the World Series on Oct. 17, 1982. The Greendale couple were married the previous day. (Ronald M. Overdahl, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) Fans took over the field at County Stadium after the Milwaukee Brewers won Game 5 of the World Series on Oct. 17, 1982. (Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Don Sutton looking distressed during Game 6 of the World Series on Oct. 19, 1982. (Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) Robin Yount (left) and Paul Molitor of the Brewers during the 1982 World Series against the St. Louis Cardinals. (Jack Orton, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) The Milwaukee area certainly is proud of its baseball team, the Brewers. Even the ice rink at Mayfair Mall has been decorated with the team’s familiar logo during the 1982 World Series. The design and appropriate cheers were etched and painted into the ice. The rink then was reflooded for skating. (Richard Brodzeller, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) The Goodyear Blimp America flew past City Hall while it was in town for the 1982 World Series. (Milwaukee Journal Sentinel) Roy Hahm held a dead chicken that he had dyed red to represent the Cardinals. Hahm carried the bird to each of the three 1982 World Series games at County Stadium. Sam LaMalfa, area supervisor of the primate buildings, dressed and held him.
